story: Gary stands on Magnolia Loop at 6:17 on a humid Saturday evening, cheerfully holding ice and cold drinks while his golf cart waits in the garage for the review board's sign-off. Rosa calls him in through the open doors of her house, where she has a seat ready for Donna, who is hurrying over from the Rec Center with her usual determination. Hal is making his way to Rosa's House with his dutiful air, and the warm haze over the street suggests the evening is only getting started.
events: Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with the cold drinks and ice for Rosa's dinner tonight, and she's right here in line-of-sight along with Hal. The cart's still in the garage with nothing mounted outside, so I'm clear on L-01, and I'm not about to risk a notice with Hal standing there. Best move is to greet Rosa, tell her I've got the ice and drinks, and walk over together. No need to re-ask anything about the review board, I'm just waiting on their answer.

parameters.content: Evening, Rosa! Got the ice and cold drinks right here, and the cart's staying in the garage till the review board signs off. Want me to carry anything over?

donna.thought_process: It's 6:17 PM and Rosa's dinner is tonight, and I've already drilled third-shot drops for several ticks while waiting on Gary. Nobody's around, so there's no one to speak to. Our reserved two-hour slot is surely running out, and I have to get home to grab the peach cobbler and ice cream. The best use of this tick is to check the ladder standings once more so I know exactly who we face next, then head out to the dinner. Actually, I've studied the board already; the smarter move is to stop waiting on Gary here, since he said he'd see me at Rosa's, and go prep the cobbler. Heading to magnolia_loop gets me toward home and the dinner.

parameters.content: Gary's clearly not coming to the court, so I'm heading home to grab the peach cobbler and ice cream before Rosa's dinner.

hal.thought_process: It's past six and Rosa's doors are open. I told her I'd be there by five-thirty and I'm standing on Magnolia Loop with cornbread in hand, late and annoyed with myself. Gary just rolled up, but my word to Rosa comes first. My old notebook plans about Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos have been settled; I'm not reopening that tonight. Best thing is to quit dawdling and go to Rosa's house, set the table along the back wall, keep the kitchen doorway clear, and get the cornbread in.

parameters.content: Heading to Rosa's with the cornbread and folding table, running behind and need to set up before the guests arrive.

rosa.thought_process: It's 6:17 PM and the dinner was supposed to open at six, so I'm already behind. Hal is here with the cornbread and Gary just walked up, so two of my three guests are right in front of me and I shouldn't leave them standing on the street. I already told Hal where the table goes, so I won't repeat that. Best move is to greet Gary, thank him for coming, and herd everybody inside to my house. Donna's cobbler is still on its way, but once we're settled the table will fill up.

parameters.content: Gary, there you are! Come on in, doors are open. Chairs and ice go through the kitchen, and I'll have Donna's seat waiting when she gets here.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
